question: What percentage of tests will be positive for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in the United States for the week ending October 10, 2026, in CDC data?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the percent of tests positive for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in the United States for the week ending 2026-10-10 in CDC's the National Respiratory and Enteric Virus Surveillance System (NREVSS) percent positivity data (data.cdc.gov dataset rgnm-fkqb), as posted on 2026-10-30.
research:
# RSV test positivity forecast: research for the week ending 2026-10-10

In the CDC dataset, RSV positivity was about 0.4-0.5% in early September 2026, roughly where it was at the same point in 2025 and 2024. In those two years it rose to 0.72% and 1.24% by the comparable week in October.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on CDC NREVSS dataset rgnm-fkqb (data.cdc.gov), using the national RSV `percent_pos` value for week ending 2026-10-10 as it stands in the 2026-10-30 posting. The dataset also has fields for tests, detections and 3-week averages. [data.cdc.gov](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json)
- Caveat: the API only serves the latest version of the data, and every row I could read was marked "posted 2026-10-30". I only report 2026 weeks that would have been published by about 2026-09-21. Their values may differ slightly from what was shown at the time.
- 2026-09-12 (latest week published by 2026-09-21): 0.37% (42,930 tests). [data.cdc.gov](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. The target week starts on 2026-10-04, after the forecast closes.
- Weekly 2026 values (week ending, percent positive), all from [data.cdc.gov](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json):
  - 06-06: 1.01
  - 06-20: 0.91
  - 07-04: 0.60
  - 07-18: 0.55
  - 08-01: 0.42
  - 08-15: 0.37
  - 08-22: 0.49
  - 08-29: 0.39
  - 09-05: 0.50
  - 09-12: 0.37
- RSV has bottomed out at about 0.4-0.5% and moves up and down a lot from week to week. The number of tests is rising (about 29k in mid-August, 43k by 09-12), which is normal for September.
- The unusually high June level (about 1%) fits a late-running 2025-26 season that extended into spring. [Pharmacy Times, 2026-03-27](https://www.pharmacytimes.com/view/late-season-rsv-surge-extends-risk-into-spring-challenging-seasonal-expectations-expert-says)

## 3. Recent news
- 2026-09-17: Detroit's respiratory virus report rated respiratory illness LOW. [Detroit](https://detroitmi.gov/sites/detroitmi.localhost/files/2026-09/City%20of%20Detroit%20-%20Respiratory%20Virus%20Report_09.17.2026.pdf)
- 2026-09-03: A British Columbia CDC report, citing US CDC data updated 2026-08-28, said US RSV activity was "very low in most areas." [BCCDC](https://www.bccdc.ca/Health-Info-Site/Documents/Respiratory_data/respiratory_surveillance_2026-09-03.pdf)
- Undated: CDC's respiratory data page says it expects the 2026-27 season to resemble last season, with similar peak hospitalizations from COVID-19, flu and RSV. [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/respiratory-viruses/data/index.html?utm_source)
- I found no CDC report specific to RSV for September 2026.

## 4. Base rates
All values are from the same dataset. [data.cdc.gov](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json)

**2025 (most similar year):**

| Week ending | % positive |
|---|---|
| 09-06 | 0.28 |
| 09-13 | 0.34 |
| 09-20 | 0.43 |
| 09-27 | 0.49 |
| 10-04 | 0.60 |
| 10-11 (comparable week) | 0.72 |
| 10-18 | 0.84 |

- Mid-September to the target week: about 2.1 times higher.

**2024:**

| Week ending | % positive |
|---|---|
| 09-07 | 0.32 |
| 09-14 | 0.42 |
| 09-21 | 0.60 |
| 09-28 | 0.79 |
| 10-05 | 1.11 |
| 10-12 (comparable week) | 1.24 |
| 10-19 | 1.91 |

- Mid-September to the target week: about 3 times higher.

**2023:**

| Week ending | % positive |
|---|---|
| 09-09 | 1.30 |
| 09-16 | 1.38 |
| 10-07 | 3.70 |
| 10-14 | 4.78 |

- 2023 started from a much higher level (about 1% in early September), so it is less comparable. Its value would have been above the question's 2.5% ceiling.

**Takeaway:**
- Over the four weeks from mid-September to the second week of October, positivity rose about 2-3.5 times in 2023-2025.
- Applying that to a 2026 level of about 0.37-0.50% (mid-September, smoothed) gives roughly 0.75-1.5%.
- The 2025 path, which CDC suggests this season will resemble, points to the low end of that range.
- Weekly noise in 2026 has been about ±0.1 percentage points.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold markets, and no published expert forecast for this exact series.
- The only related outlook is CDC's qualitative "similar to last season" statement. [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/respiratory-viruses/data/index.html?utm_source)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- CDC publishes NREVSS data weekly, usually on Fridays. Data for weeks ending 09-19, 09-26 and 10-03 will show when the seasonal rise begins.
- Recent weeks can be revised as late lab reports come in. The question uses the 2026-10-30 posting, about three weeks after the target week, so most late reports should be included by then.
- Southeastern states typically start rising first, in September and October. More use of RSV vaccines in older adults and of nirsevimab or clesrovimab in infants may hold down positivity at the start of the season.
- Rising test volume during the start of COVID and flu season could add more negative tests and push positivity down.
